Content:
FINE-GRAINED slice over CC-031 composable geometry sources and the deterministic GeneratedCreature multi-item output. Complements the coarse records creaturecreator-definition-model, creaturecreator-generation-morphology, and creaturecreator-resolved-model-world-resolver (which cover DNA shape + pipeline stage orchestration + the resolved frame resolver). Claim classification inline: [C] = Confirmed by direct source inspection of the named file plus its nearest tests; [I] = Inference/design intent not literally asserted in code.

=== GEOMETRY TYPE vs PART TYPE ===
GeometryType (Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Definition/GeometryType.cs, ns ProceduralCreature.Definition) is an enum classifying HOW a part's geometry is produced, kept semantic and ORTHOGONAL to PartType (Eye/Limb/...) [C]. PartType is deliberately never turned into a geometry taxonomy (EyeMesh/EyeSdf/...) [C per enum XML + ADR-002 §6]. Values [C]: Implicit=0 (surface derived from the implicit SDF field: Body + Shape/Limb parts), MeshAsset=1 (pre-authored mesh asset referenced by a stable key), Procedural=2 (mesh produced by a procedural MeshGenerator). Procedural is declared but NOT implemented and never produced [C: enum + ADR-002 pass-1 'procedural geometry (MeshGenerator)' deferred; no code path emits GeometryType.Procedural]. A creature definition does not store a GeometryType on a part directly; a part's geometry source is implied by which of Limb/MeshGeometry is non-null (null+null Shape primitive = implicit) [C].

=== MESH GEOMETRY + GEOMETRY ATTACHMENT (DNA layer) ===
MeshGeometry (Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Definition/MeshGeometry.cs) is a [Serializable] sealed class, the mesh-asset geometry source on a CreaturePart [C]. Fields: string MeshAssetKey (stable NAME; DNA NEVER stores a UnityEngine.Object) and GeometryAttachment Attachment = new GeometryAttachment() default [C]. Clone() deep-copies both fields (Attachment null-safe) [C]. MeshAssetKey is resolved through an EXTERNAL mesh palette/registry at generation time via an injected resolver Func<string,Mesh>; resolution is a generator-layer concern and the domain model stays portable [C: MeshGeometry XML + CreatureMeshPalette XML + generator]. This mirrors the CC-028 convention for material keys [C: doc comments].

GeometryAttachment (Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Definition/GeometryAttachment.cs) is the semantic placement intent relative to the owning part, stored in DNA so resolution/topology changes do not lose attachment intent [C]. Pass-1 carries only: UnityEngine.Vector3 Offset (default zero), Quaternion Orientation (default identity), Vector3 Scale (default one) in the part's LOCAL frame [C]. IsFinite() returns NumericValidity.IsFinite(Offset) && IsFinite(Scale) && IsFinite(Orientation) [C]. Clone() copies all three [C]. The body-surface anchor on GeometryAttachment is DELIBERATELY DEFERRED; pass 1 places mesh geometry at the part's local-space position (ADR-002 §2) [C per class XML + ADR-002].

=== CreaturePart PLUMBING + MUTUAL EXCLUSION ===
CreaturePart (Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Definition/CreaturePart.cs) carries nullable MeshGeometry parallel to nullable Limb [C]. Doc contract [C]: when MeshGeometry is non-null the part's geometry is a pre-authored mesh resolved by MeshAssetKey instead of the implicit SDF field; Shape and Limb are inert for generation; the two geometry sources (Limb chain vs MeshGeometry) are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE (validator-enforced). PartType.MirrorAcrossSymmetryPlane and ParentAttachment (BodySurfaceAnchor) coexist independently [C]. Clone() propagates MeshGeometry via MeshGeometry.Clone() (independent deep copy) [C: field + GeneratedCreatureTests.CreaturePart_Clone_CopiesMeshGeometryIndependently].

VALIDATOR (DefinitionValidator, no repair): a part with both a limb chain and MeshGeometry is rejected (ValidationCode.InvalidMeshGeometry) [C: DefinitionValidatorMeshGeometryTests.Validate_LimbAndMeshGeometry_ReportsInvalidMeshGeometry]; empty/whitespace MeshAssetKey is rejected (InvalidMeshGeometry) [C]; non-finite attachment (e.g. NaN offset) is rejected (NonFiniteMeshGeometryAttachment) [C]; a Scale component below the supported minimum is rejected (InvalidMeshGeometryScale) [C: zero x-scale (0,1,1) invalid per test]; Shape is INERT for a mesh part so a zero/invalid Shape does not raise InvalidShapeParameter [C: Validate_MeshPart_DoesNotRequireMeaningfulShape]. Validator reports invalid DNA without repair (project invariant) [I].

=== SDF COMPILER SKIPS MESH PARTS ===
SdfProgramBuilder skips resolved parts that HasMeshGeometry in the portable compile (continue) and the per-part/individual compile path filters !HasMeshGeometry, so a mesh part contributes NO Shape sphere to the implicit surface [C: SdfProgramBuilder.cs lines 450, 536]. This is why mesh geometry coexists with the implicit surface as a SEPARATE item rather than blending into it.

=== RESOLVED SNAPSHOT MESH FIELDS (single placement seam) ===
ResolvedPartSnapshot (CreaturePartWorldTransformResolver.cs) exposes HasMeshGeometry (= part.MeshGeometry != null), MeshAssetKey, GeometryOffset/Orientation/Scale (attachment normalized; defaults zero/identity/one) and GeometryPlacementToCreatureSpace = partFrameToCreatureSpace * Matrix4x4.TRS(GeometryOffset, GeometryOrientation, GeometryScale) [C]. Placement comes ONLY from the resolved snapshot (never raw DNA), per CC-051 single-seam rule; CreatureMeshGenerator reads resolvedPart.GeometryPlacementToCreatureSpace [C]. See creaturecreator-resolved-model-world-resolver for the full frame-resolver model; do not duplicate.

=== GENERATED CREATURE (multi-item output) ===
GeneratedCreature (Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Generation/GeneratedCreature.cs, ns ProceduralCreature.Generation) is the deterministic, ORDERED multi-item output of generation — a creature is no longer a single Mesh [C]. Constants [C]: string ImplicitSurfaceSourceId = "" (the implicit combined surface SourcePartId — no single part owns it) and string MirrorSuffix = "_mirror" (matches SkeletonInferrer.MirrorSuffix). Members [C]: List<GeometryItem> Geometry (get-only), int Count => Geometry.Count, Mesh MainMesh => Geometry.Count>0 ? Geometry[0].Mesh : null. Method TryFindGeometryForPart(string partId, out GeometryItem) linear-searches Geometry by SourcePartId [C].

ORDERING CONTRACT [C: code + GeneratedCreatureTests.Generate_MeshParts_OrderedBySourcePartId_AndDeterministic]: Item 0 is ALWAYS the implicit combined surface (Body + Shape/Limb parts extracted from the SDF), SourcePartId = ImplicitSurfaceSourceId "", GeometryType.Implicit, with an empty RigBindingMetadata; the generator unconditionally adds it in Assemble. Items 1..n are mesh-asset/procedural parts in ASCENDING SourcePartId (Ordinal StringComparer) so output is independent of authoring order. Mesh items are appended via AppendMeshAssetItems from data.Snapshot.PartsById.Values.Where(HasMeshGeometry).OrderBy(p => p.Id, StringComparer.Ordinal). Output is deterministic across repeated runs AND across canonicalization-equivalent inputs (CC-091 parity gate test Generate_CanonicalizationEquivalentDefinitions_ProduceEqualOutput asserts identical item count/source ids/type/vertex count/triangle count/bounds).

GeometryItem fields [C]: string SourcePartId; GeometryType GeometryType; Mesh Mesh; Mesh SourceMesh (the ORIGINAL mesh-asset source in its authored local space, never mutated); Matrix4x4 RestPlacement (authored source-to-creature rest placement; = Matrix4x4.identity default); List<MaterialRegion> MaterialRegions = new(); RigBindingMetadata RigBinding = new(). The item that ends up in Geometry[0] is the implicit combined surface.

MainMesh semantics [C]: returns item-0 mesh (the implicit combined surface). A body-only creature yields exactly one item (Generate_BodyOnly_ProducesSingleImplicitItem asserts Count==1, item0 SourcePartId=="", GeometryType.Implicit, Mesh non-null, MainMesh non-null).

=== ASSEMBLE + BUILD MESH ASSET ITEM ===
CreatureMeshGenerator.Assemble(data, meshResolver) is the Unity-Mesh boundary [C]: builds item 0 via data.MeshResult.ToUnityMesh() + mesh.SetColors(data.Colors), appends item 0 unconditionally, then calls AppendMeshAssetItems(generated, data, meshResolver) for items 1..n. AppendMeshAssetItems: for each mesh resolved part, ResolveMesh(partId, MeshAssetKey, meshResolver) -> Matrix4x4 placement = part.GeometryPlacementToCreatureSpace; adds BuildMeshAssetItem(part, sourceMesh, placement, mirror:false); if part.MirrorAcrossSymmetryPlane && data.Snapshot.SymmetryMode != SymmetryMode.None, adds a SECOND BuildMeshAssetItem with placement = MirrorUtility.ReflectTransformAcrossX(placement) and mirror:true [C]. So mirroring emits a mirrored COPY only for parts flagged MirrorAcrossSymmetryPlane under a non-None SymmetryMode; the original is always present [C: test Generate_MirroredMeshPart_EmitsMirroredCopy asserts implicit+original+mirrored, mirror only when flag+mode].

MIRROR MECHANICS [C]: ReflectTransformAcrossX(M) = Matrix4x4.Scale(-1,1,1) * M (LEFT-multiplied reflection across the creature-space X=0 plane), centralized in Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Skeleton/MirrorUtility.cs and shared with the SDF compiler and skeleton inference so a mirrored mesh-asset item lands on the same side as the mirrored implicit field. CopyTriangles reverses winding on mirrored copies (swaps index i<->i+2 per triangle) to PRESERVE outward winding after X reflection [C: Generate_MirroredMeshPart_PreservesOutwardWinding]. Mirrored item SourcePartId = part.Id + "_mirror"; GeometryType stays MeshAsset; RigBinding.IsMirrored=true [C].

BuildMeshAssetItem (per-item bake) [C]: transforms every source vertex by placement.MultiplyPoint3x4 into a NEW Mesh named "Generated_{part.Id}" (+ "_mirror" if mirrored); preserves submesh structure when source.subMeshCount>1 else single submesh; RecalculateNormals(); RecalculateBounds(); bakes the part's OWN authored appearance onto the item via AppearanceBaker.BakePart(part.Appearance, mesh.vertices, mesh.normals) — NOT nearest-surface sampling, because a mesh part is not part of the implicit SDF field (never from the Body's implicit gradient) [C: code + test Generate_MeshAssetPart_BakesAuthoredVertexColors asserts a pure-red authored color reaches every vertex with no green/blue]. The SOURCE mesh asset is never mutated; mirrored items reuse the SAME source mesh with a reflected placement [C: test asserts Geometry[1].SourceMesh == Geometry[2].SourceMesh]. Sets SourceMesh=source, RestPlacement=placement, RigBinding {SourcePartId=part.Id, ParentPartId=part.ParentId, IsMirrored=mirror} [C].

=== MATERIAL REGION (CC-028) ===
MaterialRegion {int StartIndex; int IndexCount; string MaterialKey} [C]. A mesh-asset part whose Appearance.MaterialKey is non-empty/whitespace emits ONE MaterialRegion on its item (and on its mirrored copy): StartIndex=0, IndexCount=mesh.triangles.Length, MaterialKey=part.Appearance.MaterialKey [C: BuildMeshAssetItem + test Generate_MeshPart_WithMaterialKey_PopulatesMaterialRegions]. Pass-1 region is key-only and covers the whole item (the common single-material case; doc comment calls it 'submesh 0'); resolution of the key to a UnityEngine.Material is a render-layer concern (MaterialResolver), so the generator output stays key-only and the domain stays portable [C per code comment; the 'submesh 0 / whole single-material item' precision is [I] from the comment]. ITEM 0 (implicit combined surface) DELIBERATELY gets NO MaterialRegion — it keeps the single-mesh vertex-color default path (CC-028 scope) [C: test asserts Geometry[0].MaterialRegions.Count==0]. A mesh part without a MaterialKey has no regions and keeps the part-appearance path [C].

=== RIG BINDING METADATA (CC-018 separation) ===
RigBindingMetadata {string SourcePartId; string ParentPartId; bool IsMirrored} [C]. It records the semantic rig binding — what the item FOLLOWS during animation, derived from the semantic skeleton (CC-018), never from the render mesh. Surface attachment (GeometryAttachment) and rig attachment (RigBindingMetadata) stay SEPARATE and are not collapsed into one transform [C per XML + ADR-002 §4]. Pass-1 records only source/parent part ids; resolving the EXACT bone id reuses SkeletonInferrer.ResolveParentBoneId in a LATER pass (deferred, not yet wired on the output) [C per XML + ADR-002 pass-1 'exact bone binding' deferred]. RigBinding on item 0 (implicit) is an empty RigBindingMetadata [C: Assemble].

=== MESH-ASSET KEY RESOLUTION ===
The mesh resolver is an INJECTED Func<string, Mesh> passed to Generate/Assemble [C]. CreatureMeshGenerator.ResolveMesh: if meshResolver==null, throws DomainException "Part 'X' declares mesh geometry ('key') but no mesh resolver was provided."; if meshResolver(key) returns null, throws DomainException "Mesh asset 'key' for part 'X' could not be resolved." — an unresolvable mesh-asset key is a programmer/config error and THROWS, NO SILENT DROP (per ADR-002) [C: code + tests Generate_MeshPart_WithoutResolver_ThrowsDomainException and Generate_MeshPart_WithUnresolvableKey_ThrowsDomainException]. A body-only definition with NO mesh parts never calls the resolver [C: no DomainException on body-only generate].

CreatureMeshPalette (Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Generation/CreatureMeshPalette.cs) is the runtime ScriptableObject mesh-asset registry backing the injected resolver [C]: [Serializable] Entry{string Key; Mesh Mesh}; List<Entry> Entries. TryResolve(key,out mesh) resolves via internal KeyedPaletteLookup matching entry.Key to the key ordinal (case-sensitive; rejects entries whose Mesh==null) [C]; GetUsableKeys() returns usable keys SORTED + DEDUPLICATED (ordinal) [C]; HasDuplicateKeys(out duplicateKey) reports an ordinal duplicate [C]. Creator uses ordinal key resolution (not case-insensitive): TryResolve("Eye") is false when only "eye" present [C: Editor CreatureMeshPaletteTests]. The palette is the EDITOR-side key->UnityEngine.Mesh asset holder (DNA stores only the ordinal key, so generated output can be rebuilt in Play Mode without editor-only assets) [C per palette XML]; wiring of an editor palette/resolver/authoring UI into the generator is deferred (the generator itself only accepts the injected Func) [C per ADR-002 pass-1 deferred 'editor mesh palette + resolver + authoring UI'].

=== SERIALIZATION ===
Serialization of MeshGeometry on a part is additive and covered in detail by creaturecreator-serialization-contract and the JsonDnaSerializerMeshGeometryTests fixture (reference only — meshGeometry always emitted, null for parts without one; pre-CC-031 files load unchanged; canonicalization quantizes the attachment) [C per ADR-002 Consequences; not re-derived here].

=== CURRENT-STATE SUMMARY ===
A creature = deterministic ordered List<GeometryItem>: item 0 implicit combined surface (source "", GeometryType.Implicit, no material region, empty rig binding), items 1..n mesh-asset parts ascending SourcePartId (each placed via GeometryPlacementToCreatureSpace from the resolved snapshot, mirroring via ReflectTransformAcrossX, per-part authored vertex colors, optional key-only MaterialRegion over the item, RigBindingMetadata source/parent ids + IsMirrored). Procedural geometry and exact bone binding remain un-implemented/deferred. No mesh part ever contributes to the implicit SDF. Domain model stores no UnityEngine.Object; all asset references are stable string keys resolved at generation time through injected resolvers, with unresolvable keys throwing DomainException (no silent drop).
